items.headline: Carbon County planners approve Valar's Raceway Energy Campus permit
items.what_happened: On November 12, 2026 the Carbon County, Utah planning commission approved a conditional use permit for Valar Atomics' Raceway Energy Campus, a nuclear, natural gas and data center site on 640 acres of state trust land near Wellington. One commissioner voted no. Valar says the campus will generate and use about 3 gigawatts; it plans to start with a natural gas plant and eventually build 40 to 120 nuclear reactors there. The commission took no public comment, which the county attorney said was not required.
items.why_it_matters: It is the first local land-use approval for Valar's Utah plans. The permit does not let construction start: Valar still needs a county building permit, a state air quality permit and an NRC construction permit, and the reactors come after a gas plant.
items.binding_note: A county conditional use permit, approved with conditions. It is a land-use approval, not a construction or reactor license.
